# Benchmarks

Speed and conformance of every Semantic Versions implementation against the
libraries people use today, in each language:

| Language | Package | Conformance | Compared with | Speed vs. it |
| --- | --- | :---: | --- | ---: |
| [JavaScript](../packages/parser) | `semantic-versions` (npm) | 447/447 | `semver` 390/447 | 1.3–10× |
| [Rust](../crates/semantic-versions) | `semantic-versions` (crates.io) | 447/447 | `nodejs-semver` 357/447 | 0.9–1.6× |
| [Python](../ports/python) | `semantic-versions` (PyPI) | 447/447 | `node-semver` 360/447 | 1.6–15× |
| [Go](../ports/go) | `github.com/vltpkg/semantic-versions/ports/go` (pkg.go.dev) | 447/447 | `Masterminds/semver` 342/413 | 2.5–24× |
| [Ruby](../ports/ruby) | `semantic-versions` (RubyGems) | 447/447 | `semantic_range` 360/447 | 1.6–20× |
| [Java](../ports/java) | `io.vlt:semantic-versions` (Maven Central) | 447/447 | `semver4j` 350/413 | 9.3–25× |
| [.NET](../ports/dotnet) | `SemanticVersions` (NuGet) | 447/447 | `Semver` 359/413 | 1.3–9.7× |

<!-- languages:end -->

Conformance is out of the shared suite's cases; libraries that do not expose a
desugared range string are scored on the 413 cases that do not need one. Speed
is the range of speed-ups over the compared library across the operations
below. The same results appear on [semver.xyz/libraries](https://semver.xyz/libraries/)
and in each package's README.

## Method

- **Inputs are real.** [`corpus.json`](corpus.json) holds published versions of 40
  widely used npm packages (up to 150 each, evenly spaced across their history)
  and 2,000 dependency ranges those packages actually declare, fetched from the
  public registry. Every language runs the same corpus.
- **Same answers.** Every implementation is checked against the JavaScript
  reference on the whole corpus (validation, desugaring, membership,
  resolution and sort order) as well as on the conformance suite.
- **Same work for everyone.** Range operations are measured only on ranges every
  library in that language's comparison accepts, so no library is timed on
  input it rejects early. Libraries with their own range syntax (Cargo's
  `semver`, python-semver, `blang/semver`, `Gem::Version`, `java-semver`) are
  compared on versions only.
- **Idiomatic use.** JavaScript is measured through each library's string API
  (`satisfies(version, range)`, `maxSatisfying(list, range)`, `sort(list)`),
  which is how it is called there. Every other language parses once and then
  compares parsed values. Compare numbers within a language, not across
  languages.
- **Median of many samples.** Each operation warms up (200 ms; 1 s on the JVM
  and .NET so the JIT settles), then runs 15 samples of 250 ms; the tables
  report the median time per operation.
- **Conformance** comes from the shared suite in [`../conformance`](../conformance),
  scored per feature. A library that does not implement a feature (contexts,
  channels) fails those cases by design; that is the point of the table.

## Run

| Language | From | Command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JavaScript | repository root | `vlt run bench -w packages/parser` |
| Rust | `crates/semantic-versions` | `cargo bench --bench compare` |
| Python | `ports/python` | `pip install node-semver semver && python bench/compare.py` |
| Go | `ports/go/bench` | `go run .` |
| Ruby | `ports/ruby` | `bundle install && bundle exec rake bench` |
| Java | `ports/java` | `bench/run.sh` |
| .NET | `ports/dotnet` | `dotnet run -c Release --project bench` |
| PHP | `ports/php` | `composer install && composer bench` |

Each runner writes `results/<language>.json`; `--quick` (`-quick` for Go and
.NET) does a fast run that does not write results. Then refresh the README
tables with `node benchmarks/report.mjs`; the site reads the JSON at build time.

## JavaScript

### Speed

| Operation | `semantic-versions@1.0.0` | `semver@7.8.6` | semantic-versions vs semver |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Parse a version | **78.3 ns** | 231 ns | **3.0× faster** |
| Sort versions | **350 ns** | 3.58 µs | **10× faster** |
| Parse a range | **4.22 µs** | 5.61 µs | **1.3× faster** |
| satisfies(version, range) | **414 ns** | 837 ns | **2.0× faster** |
| Resolve a range | **14.5 µs** | 45.9 µs | **3.2× faster** |

<sub>Median time per operation (lower is better) on 5,398 published versions and 1,996 dependency ranges from the npm registry. Node.js 22.23.5 · Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.30GHz · linux x64 · 2026-11-19.</sub>

### Conformance

| Semantic Versions feature | `semantic-versions` | `semver` |
| --- | :---: | :---: |
| Version grammar <br><sub>Valid and invalid versions per the BNF</sub> | ✓ 81/81 | ✓ 81/81 |
| No coercion <br><sub>Rejects `v1.2.3`, `=1.2.3`, `1.2.3pre`, …</sub> | ✓ 11/11 | ◐ 10/11 |
| Precedence <br><sub>Major, minor, patch and pre-release ordering</sub> | ✓ 32/32 | ✓ 32/32 |
| Build precedence <br><sub>A build ranks above its release: `1.0.0 < 1.0.0+b`</sub> | ✓ 10/10 | ◐ 1/10 |
| Ranges <br><sub>Comparators, `\|\|`, x-ranges, `~`, `^`, hyphen ranges</sub> | ✓ 199/199 | ✓ 199/199 |
| Approximate ranges <br><sub>The pessimistic operator `~>`</sub> | ✓ 17/17 | ✓ 17/17 |
| Pre-release channels <br><sub>`^1.0.0-rc` admits `rc.*`, never `beta`</sub> | ✓ 44/44 | ◐ 33/44 |
| Pre-release wildcards <br><sub>`X.Y.Z-*` and `*-*` opt in explicitly</sub> | ✓ 14/14 | ◐ 2/14 |
| Build channels <br><sub>`^1.0.0+win` admits `+win.*` builds only</sub> | ✓ 24/24 | ◐ 12/24 |
| Contexts <br><sub>`npm:react@18.2.0`, `npm:react@^18`</sub> | ✓ 15/15 | ◐ 3/15 |
| **All cases** | **447/447** | **390/447** |

<sub>Cases from the shared conformance suite in [`conformance/`](https://github.com/vltpkg/semantic-versions/tree/main/conformance), drawn from the specification. ✓ all pass · ◐ some pass · ✗ none pass.</sub>

| range->test(version) | **169 ns** | 621 ns | 474 ns | **3.7× faster** |
| Resolve a range | **26.7 µs** | 101.9 µs | 71.0 µs | **3.8× faster** |

<sub>Median time per operation (lower is better) on 5,398 published versions and 797 dependency ranges from the npm registry. PHP 8.3.6 · Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.30GHz · linux x86_64 · 2026-11-19. `composer/semver`: Composer's model differs by design: versions normalize to four parts with stability flags (1.0.0-rc.1 becomes 1.0.0.0-RC1), builds are dropped, and pre-release names outside alpha, beta, RC and patch are rejected. Versions are scored on parsing to the same value.</sub>
